record.title: Attempt on Fourier entropy versus total influence
record.statement: ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Fourier entropy versus total influence exact calculation or structural obstruction Result: Discarding the Boolean constraint destroys the claim: the probability measure uniform on the n singleton subsets has entropy log2(n) but mean subset size1. It cannot be the squared spectrum of a Boolean function when n>=2. Check: If all Fourier mass were on singletons, f=sum_i a_i*x_i with a_i=plus/minus1/sqrt(n). In f^2 the coefficient of x_i*x_j is2*a_i*a_j, nonzero for distinct i,j, whereas Boolean f requires f^2=1. This independently exhibits the violated Fourier convolution identity. Obstruction: Entropy versus mean cardinality alone is insufficient. Any proof must use the nonlinear identities imposed by f^2=1; no dimension-free inequality exploiting all of them is obtained.
assumptions: Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0162-fourier-entropy-versus-total-influence
